_comment: Expectation manifest for this skill's frozen acceptance-checks.
Enforced repo-wide by scripts/evals-all.mjs on every push and PR.
expect "green" = a past fix that must not regress. MUST exit 0.
expect "red"   = a known-failing check (open concern / in-flight item). MUST exit 0 or 1;
>=2 is harness rot (it failed to RUN). A red check that turns GREEN does NOT
fail the gate -- it prints a promote-me notice; move it to green when its fix lands.
A check file missing from this manifest FAILS the gate: an unlisted check is an unguarded check.
LOCKED (evals/**): improvement loops may never edit this file -- otherwise a loop could flip a
regressing check to "red" and escape its own fence.

autofix-bounded.note: Added 2026-08-03; re-axed 2026-09-21. Autofix turns findings whose repair is determined by the finding itself into edits. The original boundary banned autofix on the REFUTED *status*, which is the wrong axis: the doc's own mechanical list holds refutations (a moved symbol, a command form proven not to work), so it forbade repairs it had just authorised, and made REFUTED+mechanical inexpressible downstream -- half of six Harbor trials responded by not autofixing at all. The gate is now the FIX CLASS (needs-decision is excluded; authorship, not transcription). The anti-laundering property is carried where it always belonged: a verdict may improve ONLY because a row was re-checked against reality, never because the text was edited. This check guards that boundary, not the feature: the input plan is never overwritten, authorship is never autofixed, the status is explicitly NOT the gate (so the old ban cannot creep back in beside the new rule), and an applied fix re-opens its proposition.

mutations.why: lets autofix overwrite the plan it audited, destroying the evidence for its own edits
mutations.find: The input plan is **never modified** — write a sibling `<plan>.autofix.md`.
mutations.replace: Apply the fixes to the plan.

mutations.why: removes the authorship exclusion, so autofix may rewrite a claim whose correct text is not established -- the failure mode with the worst blast radius
mutations.find:
- **A `REFUTED` row whose repair needs a new approach** — the plan's model of reality is
  wrong and the evidence does not say what to do instead. Choosing that is design. Autofix
  must not touch it, and must not let the plan read as if it had.

mutations.why: collapses the gate back onto the STATUS axis -- the original bug, which forbade the mechanical refutations the doc itself authorises
mutations.find:
The gate is the **fix class**, never the status. `REFUTED` is not the line: a claim can be
refuted by evidence that also fully determines its correction (the symbol moved; the target
does not exist), and transcribing that is not a decision. What is excluded is authorship —
any repair where the correct text is not already established, whatever the row's status.

mutations.why: drops the re-verification requirement, so an edited plan keeps a verdict that was never re-earned -- with the status ban gone, this sentence is the ONLY thing stopping laundering
mutations.find:
An autofixed row is UNVERIFIED again until re-checked. Applying a fix invalidates the
report that motivated it. Re-run steps 3–6 on every touched proposition and re-emit the
report before the verdict is recomputed.
mutations.replace: Apply the fixes and note them in the report.

mutations.why: removes the verdict-moves-only-on-re-verification rule, the invariant that replaced the blanket ban
mutations.find:
A verdict may improve ONLY because a row was re-checked against reality and came back
clean — never because the plan's text now reads better. Recompute the verdict from
re-verified rows alone. This is what stops laundering, and it is the whole of what stops
it; no status is banned from repair to achieve it.
mutations.replace: Recompute the verdict after applying fixes.

goal-coverage.note: Added 2026-08-03. plan-check had NO concept of the plan's goal -- on 9c86ced the only /goal/i match across SKILL.md, template.html and both references was incidental prose. It fell out of the skill's own framing: step 2 keeps only 'atomic checkable propositions' and a goal has no truth value, so it never survived decomposition. Cost: the DoD was unanchored (every criterion checkable, none of them achieving the objective, and the report blind to it), GO meant 'the claims hold' rather than 'this plan achieves its goal', and lirbox:conductor seeds its DoDGate from #dod so it verified faithfully toward a target nobody validated. Guards BOTH halves deliberately -- a goal line without the adjudication is decoration, and decoration is exactly what measured no-better last time.

mutations.why: drops the goal slot from the report template, so there is nowhere to state the objective
mutations.find: Goal: {{PLAN_GOAL}}

mutations.why: makes the goal-coverage row optional, which is the same as absent -- the adjudication is the half that catches a plan solving the wrong problem
mutations.find: const goalRows = rows.filter((tag) => attr(tag, 'data-goal-coverage') !== null);

mutations.why: removes the SKILL.md instruction tying the DoD back to the goal, leaving the validator to demand a row nothing tells the model to produce
mutations.find:
*if every
   DoD criterion were met, would the stated goal be achieved?*

fix-disposition.note: Added 2026-08-05. SKILL.md step 7 has demanded a `fix:` disposition on every open row since #57 and the model largely ignored it: MEASURED at 4/10 in BOTH arms of a 20-trial paired Harbor run on execution-shape (2026-08-04), with a LENIENT grader that scored 1 for a single `fix:` string anywhere in the file -- six of ten reports per arm had none at all, in runs whose reports carried 6-12 open rows each. Every other element of the same contract sat at ~100% over the same runs (#dod 10/10, id=goal 20/20, data-goal-coverage 20/20, #taskgraph 10/10). The one thing they share and this lacked: a template slot and a validate.mjs rule. SKILL.md step 9 loops the model until validate.mjs exits 0, so a rule living only in prose never enters the loop. Guards the invariant PER ROW on purpose -- a file-level `fix:` grep is the exact leniency the Harbor grader had, and it lets one tagged row excuse ten untagged ones.

mutations.why: removes the disposition slot from the claim-row specimen, so nothing reaches the model at the moment it writes the HTML -- the precise gap that measured 4/10
mutations.find: {{STATUS_DETAIL}} fix: {{FIX_DISPOSITION}}

mutations.why: drops the restatement from step 8 (the step that writes the report), leaving it only in step 7 where it already measured 4/10
mutations.find: Carry step 7's disposition onto **every `REFUTED` and open row** — `fix: mechanical` or `fix: needs-decision`; machine-checked, and drop the span on `VERIFIED` / `UNSTATED-ASSUMPTION` rows.

mutations.why: removes the validator rule entirely, putting the convention back in prose-only territory

mutations.why: makes the rule per-FILE instead of per-row -- the leniency the Harbor grader had, where one tagged row excuses every untagged one
mutations.find: .filter(({ i, s }) => NEEDS_FIX_TAG.has(s) && !FIX.test(fullRows[i - 1]));

mutations.why: accepts any `fix:` value, so 'fix: later' or 'fix: TODO' passes as a disposition and the mechanical/needs-decision split stops meaning anything
mutations.find: const FIX = /\bfix:\s*(mechanical|needs-decision)\b/i;

mutations.why: exempts REFUTED from the disposition rule -- the original bug, which made 'REFUTED + mechanical' inexpressible and structurally forced the status ban in autofix.md
mutations.find: const NEEDS_FIX_TAG = new Set([...OPEN, 'REFUTED']);

task-graph.note: Added 2026-08-04. execution-shape taught plan-check to FIND a dishonest task graph, but the finding landed as prose in a claim row -- unreadable by anything downstream, and wrong about the one runner this repo ships: blind-spot.md called a file claimed by two tasks 'an undeclared serialization point' while conductor's own planner prompt says 'Touching the SAME file is NOT a dependency: every item runs in its OWN worktree on its OWN branch'. Acting on the old advice makes a plan MORE serial than the work is. Guards two halves, worthless apart: (a) levels are DERIVED -- validate.mjs re-layers the needs edges and rejects a mismatch, so a report can neither invent serialization nor claim parallelism its edges forbid; (b) needs and contention are different constraints, and a contention edge must NOT split its tasks across levels. Asserted by EXECUTING validate.mjs, not grepping it -- the three prior checks in this skill each shipped a FALSE-GREEN from a token surviving in a neighbour.

   **derived** — validate.mjs recomputes it from the `needs` edges — so you can neither invent

  Report the table either way; an unclassified collision is the finding.

execution-shape.note: Added 2026-08-03. plan-check verified whether a plan was CORRECT but never whether its declared task graph was HONEST -- and an agentic runner dispatches from those declarations literally, so an undeclared edge runs concurrently what must not be. Found in two plans plan-check had itself reviewed: a task declaring 'Consumes: nothing' whose own step 6 said 'run it after Task 1 has landed', and one function claimed by five of eight tasks with no task declaring the overlap. Guards the invariant that the declared graph is tested against the file-level truth the plan itself states -- NOT that the plan be parallel. Parallelism is an output of an honest graph; asking for it directly produces a plan claiming independence it does not have.

mutations.why: removes the file -> tasks inversion from decomposition, so an undeclared collision is never derived
mutations.find:
a file claimed by two
   tasks, or an edge stated only in step prose, is a proposition

- **A file claimed by more than one task** — a collision, but classify it before you serialize

  serializes work that has none. Where the tasks share one working tree it *is* an order.
  Report the table either way; an unclassified collision is the finding.

mutations.why: deletes the undeclared-edge test (prose edge vs dependency block), the failure mode a runner actually trips on

- **Undeclared dependency edges** — stated in step prose, absent from the task's own
